title: Tidewater Hours
description: A slow walk along one estuary through a full year of tides. Each episode stays in one place long enough to hear it change. Recorded outdoors, mostly at dawn.

title: The Long Rehearsal
description: Conversations from the weeks before an opening night. Directors, stagehands and understudies talk about the part nobody sees. Every season follows a different production.

title: Quiet Machinery
description: How ordinary objects actually work, one mechanism at a time. A zip, a kettle switch, a lift door. Short, precise and oddly calming.

title: Paper Compass
description: Trips planned with nothing but a paper map and a single day. Wrong turns are kept in. Each episode ends wherever the day ran out.

title: Small Weather
description: The weather of a single garden, a single street, a single window. Fog, frost and the first warm hour of spring. Ten minutes, once a fortnight.

title: Ninth Street Signal
description: A serialised story about a pirate radio station that only broadcasts at night. Nobody knows who runs it. Twelve chapters, each one a single broadcast.

title: Static Garden
description: Field recordings of radios left on in greenhouses, sheds and allotments. Music drifts in and out between the weather reports. Nobody is ever interviewed.

title: Two Chairs
description: One host, one guest, two chairs and no notes. Guests are asked to bring a single object and explain it. The rest follows from there.

title: Fieldnotes at Noon
description: Lunch-break conversations with people who keep unusual notebooks. Beekeepers, bus drivers, choir masters. Recorded wherever they happen to be at midday.

title: Answering Machine
description: Listeners leave a question on a real answering machine. Two hosts play it back and argue about the answer. No question is too small.

title: The Tin Kettle
description: Kitchen talk over a boiling kettle. Cooks describe one dish from memory, without a recipe in front of them. The dish is made after the episode, never during.

title: Late Draft
description: Writers read the version they threw away. Then they explain what changed and why. Sometimes the discarded draft wins.

title: Practical Ghosts
description: Local legends checked against the paperwork. Land registries, parish records and old newspapers. Most ghosts turn out to have an address.
